builder_plan.scenario: A self-hosted model uses more compute or memory than your workload can justify.
builder_plan.change: Check for a usable pruned checkpoint and runtime support before attempting model surgery.
builder_plan.baseline: The original unpruned model at the same precision, context, and load.
steps: Locate the paper's implementation and check its license, model support, data needs, and hardware requirements. Stop here if you cannot obtain the required artifacts.
Save a small set of representative product tasks and expected outcomes. Keep evaluation tasks out of any training or tuning, and choose quality and cost limits before running.
Run the baseline and the proposed change on identical inputs. Keep other settings fixed and repeat paired runs to expose variation.
Save per-task outputs, failures, timings, and all usage costs. Review regressions before expanding the test.
builder_plan.measure: Task quality, actual GPU memory, serving throughput, and preparation cost.
builder_plan.decision: Keep the change only if it meets your preselected quality and latency limits and improves the metric you care about after setup and operating costs. Otherwise retain the baseline. This is an exploration plan, not a validated recommendation.

title: Compression Trinity: Exploring Sparsity, Quantization, and Low-Rank Approximations for LLM Compression
summary: Replaces isolated pruning, quantization, or low-rank methods with joint pipelines where low-rank adapters compensate for pruning and quantization losses. Implementation spans five methods, MKOR, SLoPe, OPTIMA, PATCH, and SLiM, without an indicated mature ready-to-use artifact; several need fine-tuning budgets or pretraining access. Reproducing the thesis's columnwise optimal reconstruction or mathematically derived adapters requires substantial engineering and is not plug-and-play.
rationale: The reported gains are spread across five thesis methods without a ready artifact; a small 24 GB setup is likely better served initially by packaged GPTQ/AWQ and LoRA.
technique: Compression Trinity: joint sparsity, quantization, low rank

claims.statement: Replaces isolated pruning, quantization, or low-rank methods with joint pipelines where low-rank adapters compensate for pruning and quantization losses. Implementation spans five methods, MKOR, SLoPe, OPTIMA, PATCH, and SLiM, without an indicated mature ready-to-use artifact; several need fine-tuning budgets or pretraining access. Reproducing the thesis's columnwise optimal reconstruction or mathematically derived adapters requires substantial engineering and is not plug-and-play.

PATCH reports up to 1.38x speedup with dynamic hybrid sparsity; SLiM reports +5.66% accuracy over the state of the art; MKOR reports 1.85x convergence relative to KFAC; SLoPe reports 1.25x faster training.
